_comment: Parts the rules engine can blame. 'kind' says whether it is the PC/setup, the firmware, or the phone. 'checks' are the next bench steps shown to the tech, in order. {usb_chip} is filled in per model. A check starting with 'stacked:' is only shown for two-layer (sandwich) boards; 'faceid:' only for Face ID models.

usb_link.label: USB connection (cable, PC port, hub)
checks: Use a known-good Apple cable straight into a rear USB port on the PC (no hub, keyboard or front-panel port).
Run it again. If it stops somewhere different, the connection is the likely cause.

pc_drivers.label: This PC's Apple driver or Mobile Device Service
checks: Restart 'Apple Mobile Device Service' in Windows Services, or repair the Apple Devices app / iTunes.
Unplug and replug the phone, then run the ready check again.

network_signing.label: Network path to Apple's signing server
checks: Confirm the ready check can reach gs.apple.com.
Remove any gs.apple.com lines from C:\Windows\System32\drivers\etc\hosts.
Pause third-party firewall or antivirus software and try again.

firmware_signing.label: Firmware no longer signed by Apple for this phone
checks: Choose a build Apple still signs. The firmware list only offers those; 'Latest signed' is always safe.

ipsw_file.label: The IPSW file (corrupt or wrong model)
checks: Re-download the IPSW; the app checks its checksum.
Confirm the IPSW lists this exact model identifier.

phone_state.label: Phone state (locked, not trusted, or wrong mode)
checks: Put the phone into Recovery or DFU mode by hand (DFU helper) and start again.
If it boots normally, unlock it and tap Trust first.

usb_port_ic.label: Charge port and USB data path
checks: Try a known-good charge port / dock flex.
Compare the USB data lines in diode mode against a known-good board.
If it charges but never shows up on USB, suspect the USB data chip ({usb_chip}).

early_boot.label: CPU, RAM or main power rails
checks: Power the board from a DC supply and note the boot current pattern (add it under Bench reading).
Check the main power rails for shorts in diode mode.
Try DFU twice on a direct port; failing at the same hop both times points to the board.

nand.label: NAND storage (chip, its power rails, CPU-to-NAND link)
checks: Diode-check the NAND power rails against a known-good board.
Run once more on a different cable and port. Failing at the same step or percent confirms storage.
If the customer needs their data, stop restoring: every attempt writes to the NAND.

i2c_peripheral.label: A peripheral holding the I2C bus (often a front sensor, earpiece or Face ID flex)
checks: Disconnect the front sensor / earpiece / Face ID flex and other removable flexes, then run again.
If it now gets further, reconnect parts one at a time to find the one that stops it.
Inspect connectors and modules for corrosion, especially after liquid exposure.

baseband.label: Baseband (modem section)
checks: Measure the baseband PMU output rails.
stacked: Inspect the interposer joint between the two board layers for separation or corrosion.
A baseband fault normally repeats at the same step; one more run confirms it.

secure_element.label: Secure Element / NFC for Apple Pay
checks: Inspect the Secure Element and NFC area for liquid damage or prior rework.
Run once more; repeating at Updating SE firmware confirms the SE path.

nfc_controller.label: NFC controller (Stockholm)
checks: Inspect the NFC controller area and its antenna connection.
Run once more; repeating at the Stockholm step confirms it.

faceid.label: Face ID / biometric camera module and its flex (Savage, Yonkers)
checks: Run again with a known-good front sensor / Face ID flex if you have one.
Inspect the flood illuminator and dot projector area for corrosion.
Ask whether the module or flex was replaced; aftermarket parts can fail this step.

touchid.label: Touch ID sensor and its cable
checks: Inspect the Touch ID flex and connector.
Touch ID is paired to the board; a swapped sensor will not pair.

uwb.label: Ultra Wideband chip (Rose)
checks: Inspect the UWB area for liquid damage or rework.
Run once more; repeating at Updating Rose confirms it.

battery.label: Battery, gas gauge or battery management
checks: Fit a known-good battery charged above 50% and reseat the connector.
Aftermarket batteries commonly fail these steps.

sep.label: Secure Enclave / secure storage pairing
checks: Ask whether the CPU, NAND or secure storage chip was replaced or reworked.
Mismatched paired parts fail SEP steps on every attempt.

factory_data.label: Factory data (syscfg / FDR)
checks: If the NAND was replaced, confirm the serial number, Wi-Fi MAC and Bluetooth MAC were programmed.
Run again on a stable internet connection; factory data is fetched from Apple.

usbc_controller.label: USB-C port controller
checks: Try a known-good USB-C port flex and a different USB-C cable.
Inspect the port controller area for liquid damage.

other.label: Another firmware-updated part
checks: Note the step name in the log and compare with earlier cases in History.
